This notebook tests the hypothesis that age by sex trajectories in US mortality data can be used to identify physiological vs external influences on disease incidence.
Sex-specific cancers that are solely driven by biology should cluster more frequently with more biologically driven diseases, whereas external causes should cluster more frequently with environmentally (gender) driven diseases.

Load package and data
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(reshape2)
data_GACod <- read.csv("1999-2019_Gender_byAge45andup_10-year-groups_byCauseofDeath.csv",header=T)
```

Organizing Mortality Data.
```{r}
data1 <- janitor::clean_names(data_GACod)
data1<-rename(data1, age = ten_year_age_groups_code)
data1<-rename(data1, ucd = underlying_cause_of_death)
data1<-rename(data1, ucd_code = underlying_cause_of_death_code)
data1<-rename(data1, CR = crude_rate)
data1<-rename(data1, CRSE = crude_rate_standard_error)
data1 <- data1[!is.na(data1$population), ]#remove empty rows
data1$cat_code<-substr(data1$ucd_code,1,3)
length(unique(data1$cat_code))
```
Aggregate number of deaths by cat_code and age group.
```{r}
deaths_by_age_code<-data1 %>% 
  group_by(age, cat_code) %>% 
  summarise(deaths = sum(deaths))
deathcheck<-dcast(deaths_by_age_code,cat_code ~ age)
```
Identify causes of death that do not have sufficient deaths to reliably calculate mortality rates for QCing the data. Typically CDC sets this value at 20 deaths per year to calculate reliable mortality. However we have two groups to consider, males and females. Somewhere within 400-800 deaths should give reliable data. We do not do this by sex however as doing so we would lose codes where males or females have extremely low deaths in comparison to the other group.
```{r}
deathcheck$mincheck<-apply(deathcheck[,2:6], 1, FUN = min)
keep400<-as.data.frame(deathcheck[deathcheck$mincheck>=400,])
keep400 <- keep400[complete.cases(keep400),]
reliable400<-unique(keep400$cat_code)
```
Cutoff of 400 (20 deaths per age group per year) yields 299 codes

Remove unreliable codes.
```{r}
overlap1<-(data1$cat_code %in% reliable400)
data1$remove<-overlap1
codes_keep<-data1[data1$remove != "FALSE",]
codes_keep<-codes_keep[,-c(2,3,6)]
length(unique(codes_keep$cat_code))
```
Now aggregate by gender, code and age group.
```{r}
deaths_by_age_code_gender<-codes_keep %>% 
  group_by(age, gender,cat_code) %>% 
  summarise(deaths = sum(deaths))
Ndeaths<- sum(deaths_by_age_code_gender$deaths)

pop<-codes_keep %>% 
  group_by(age, gender) %>% 
  summarise(population = population)
pop<-distinct(pop)
```
```{r}
deaths_by_age_code_gender<-dcast(deaths_by_age_code_gender, gender + cat_code ~ age)

deaths_by_age_code_gender<-merge(deaths_by_age_code_gender,codes_keep[,c(8:9)],by="cat_code")
deaths_by_age_code_gender<-distinct(deaths_by_age_code_gender)
deaths_by_age_code_gender<-deaths_by_age_code_gender[,-c(8)]

deaths_by_age_code_gender$mincheck<-apply(deaths_by_age_code_gender[,3:7], 1, FUN = min)
deaths_by_age_code_gender$avgcheck<-apply(deaths_by_age_code_gender[,3:7], 1, FUN = mean)

table(deaths_by_age_code_gender$cat_code)
```
Causes of death with one gender missing are female- or male- specific. Put zero deaths in for the gender that cannot die of these causes. .01 will prevent NaN's from resulting later from log correction. C51-C58 are female organ cancers; C60-C63 are male organ cancers.
```{r}
Fspecific<-c("C51","C52","C53","C54","C55","C56","C57","C58")
Mspecific<-c("C60","C61","C62","C63")
overlap1<-(deaths_by_age_code_gender$cat_code %in% Fspecific)
deaths_by_age_code_gender$Fspecific<-overlap1
overlap1<-(deaths_by_age_code_gender$cat_code %in% Mspecific)
deaths_by_age_code_gender$Mspecific<-overlap1
codes_Fspecific<-deaths_by_age_code_gender[deaths_by_age_code_gender$Fspecific == "TRUE",]
codes_Mspecific<-deaths_by_age_code_gender[deaths_by_age_code_gender$Mspecific == "TRUE",]
codes_Fspecific[,c(3:7)]<-1
codes_Fspecific$gender<-"Male"
codes_Mspecific[,c(3:7)]<-1
codes_Mspecific$gender<-"Female"
deaths_by_age_code_gender<-rbind(deaths_by_age_code_gender,codes_Fspecific,codes_Mspecific)
deaths_by_age_code_gender$Fspecific<-NULL
deaths_by_age_code_gender$Mspecific<-NULL
table(deaths_by_age_code_gender$cat_code)
Ncodes<-length(unique(deaths_by_age_code_gender$cat_code))
```
Data is now complete.

Calculate log mortality by sex.
```{r}
melt<-melt(deaths_by_age_code_gender, id=c("cat_code","gender"))
melt<-rename(melt, age = variable)
melt<-rename(melt, deaths = value)
melt<-merge(melt,pop,by=c("gender","age"))
melt$MR<-melt$deaths/melt$population*100000
melt$logMR<-log(melt$MR)
logMR<-melt
length(unique(logMR$cat_code))
```

Calculate sex differences in log mortality by age and cause of death.
```{r}
logMR_by_gender<-dcast(melt[,c(1,2,3,7)], cat_code + age ~ gender)
logMR_by_gender$Diff<-logMR_by_gender$Male-logMR_by_gender$Female
length(unique(logMR_by_gender$cat_code))
```

Centering data for clustering.
```{r}
logMRdiff_by_age<-dcast(logMR_by_gender[,c(1,2,5)], cat_code ~ age)
logMRdiff_by_age$cat_code->row.names(logMRdiff_by_age)
logMRdiff_by_age$cat_code<-NULL
logMRdiff_by_cat<-as.data.frame(t(logMRdiff_by_age))
logMRdiff_by_cat_centered<-as.data.frame(scale(logMRdiff_by_cat,center=T,scale=F))
logMRdiff_by_cat_centered_scaled<-as.data.frame(scale(logMRdiff_by_cat,center=T,scale=T))
logMRdiff_by_age_centered<-as.data.frame(t(logMRdiff_by_cat_centered))
logMRdiff_by_age_centered_scaled<-as.data.frame(t(logMRdiff_by_cat_centered_scaled))
```

extended pairs code
```{r}
panel.cor <- function(x, y, digits = 2, prefix = "", cex.cor, ...)
{
  usr <- par("usr"); on.exit(par(usr))
  par(usr = c(0, 1, 0, 1))
  r <- abs(cor(x, y,use="pairwise.complete.obs"))
  txt <- format(c(r, 0.123456789), digits = digits)[1]
  txt <- paste0(prefix, txt)
  if(missing(cex.cor)) cex.cor <- 0.8/strwidth(txt)
  text(0.5, 0.5, txt, cex = cex.cor * r)
}
```


exploring relationships between variables
```{r}
pairs(logMR_by_gender[,3:5],lower.panel=panel.cor)
pairs(logMRdiff_by_age,lower.panel=panel.cor,main="log Mortality sexdiff by age, uncentered")
pairs(logMRdiff_by_age_centered,lower.panel=panel.cor,main="log Mortality sexdiff by age, centered")
pairs(logMRdiff_by_age_centered_scaled,lower.panel=panel.cor,main="log Mortality sexdiff by age, centered and scaled")
```
